description_and_math: Shared library imported by every subgen script. Defines: (1) gene set = protein-coding mRNA cistrons (every cistron with an associated monomer), in cistron order. (2) STRICT successful-lineage filter: for seed s, doubling time T(s,gen)=(time[-1]-time[0])/60 min; n_at_180(s)=#{gen: T>=179.99}; is_successful(s)=completed_all(s) AND n_at_180(s)==0 (divided every generation AND never hit the 180-min length cap). (3) DEFINITION 5, ALWAYS THE CI FORM: lambda(s,g)=mean over lineage s cells of S(c,g), where S(c,g)=Sum_t countRnaCistronSynthesized[t,g]; mean(g)=mean_s lambda; SE(g)=std(lambda,ddof=1)/sqrt(N); CI=mean +/- 1.96*SE; classify_def5_ci/_classify_ci: never_expressed iff mean=0, subgen iff ci_high<1, not_subgen iff ci_low>1, else possibly_subgen. pooled_mean() is reported as a DESCRIPTIVE statistic only -- a point estimate compared against 1 is a diagnostic, never a label. (The old classify_def5_threshold() encoding that rule was REMOVED, along with the unused load_lineage_success().) Also defines: SEED_RANGE (0-128); TIMEPOINTS_TO_SAMPLE + sample_per_seed(n_lineages) for the subsample scripts (divides by lineages ACTUALLY sampled, fixing the /128 bug); CURATED_PANELS / curated_panel() holding the 10-gene and anaerobic monomer panels; PALETTE / CAT_LABEL / CATEGORIES for the 4 def5_CI categories; git_info / load_sim_metadata / sim_metadata_block / write_run_metadata for shared provenance; load_def5_table / load_def5_categories, which read a per-gene def-5 table under EITHER column spelling (category or def5_CI_category; gene_id or gene_name); subsample_seed_timepoints() and collapse_trna_to_aa(); load_lineage_success_rows(); load_raw_* readers and canonical_def5_classification().

Reads each successful cell (gen>=8) simOut ONCE and persists per-cell matrices so all downstream def5/Task-4 analyses avoid re-reading simOut. Per cell/gene computes S(c,g)=Sum_t countRnaCistronSynthesized[t,g], max_t mRNA_cistron_counts, max_t monomerCounts, and the time-weighted fraction of the cell cycle at zero protein. Uses compute_lineage_success for the strict flag. Skips the synth matrix (with warning) if countRnaCistronSynthesized is absent. NOW ALSO persists per-generation doubling times (free -- compute_lineage_success already walked every Main/time). Outputs use the FIXED basename subgen_raw_extract, not plotOutFileName, so consumers can always find them. Run this FIRST: jobs 02 and 04 depend on it.

description_and_math: Independent reference implementation of def5_CI computed directly from simOut. lambda(s,g)=mean over lineage cells of S(c,g); mean/std/se/CI across lineages; classify by CI vs 1. Produces both all-lineage and successful-lineage tables plus diagnostic plots. It shares the CLASSIFIER with subgen_common (so the rule cannot drift) but keeps its OWN simOut pass on purpose: that independence is what makes it a cross-check on subgen_raw_extract.py's reduction. _crosscheck_raw_extract() now runs that comparison automatically whenever the raw extraction is present, printing the max |mean difference| and warning loudly on any category disagreement. On sim set 1 the two agree exactly (max difference 0 across all 4309 genes). DO NOT rebase this onto the raw extraction -- the saved pass is not worth losing the check.

THE canonical per-gene table. Classifies each protein-coding gene by def5_CI over successful lineages. Its column set is now the UNION of the two tables that previously held the same classification under different names, and the key columns are emitted under BOTH spellings (gene_name/cistron_name/protein_name/def5_CI_category AND gene_id/cistron_id/protein_id/category), so sc.load_def5_categories() reads this file or subgen_definition5_lineage_ci_pergene_successful.tsv interchangeably -- verified to agree gene-for-gene on all 4309 genes. Added columns: n_lineages, std, se (from the same stats dict) and p_mrna_present_def1 = (max_mrna[is_successful] > 0).mean(axis=0), which reproduces the legacy subgenerational_expression_table.py p_expressed column from the already-loaded max-mRNA matrix -- no extra simOut pass, a clean denominator, and gated on strict-successful lineages, so it is the more correct version of that number. Also reports the pooled def5 mean and Definition-4 probability p_any_synth(g) as descriptive statistics.

Figure only. Scatter of Definition-4 frequency p_any_synth(g) (y) vs gene rank by def5_CI mean(g) (x), colored by def5_CI category; plus a log-x histogram of mean(g) with a reference line at 1 transcript/gen. Replaces the disabled legacy transcriptFrequency.py.

Figure only. Selects the 12 subgen genes with the largest def5_CI mean(g); reads their mRNA + monomer time-series from simOut and plots per-generation traces, each generation normalized to unit width: x(t)=gen_number+(t-t_start)/(t_end-t_start).

Reads the raw extraction, restricts to strict-successful lineages, and for ALL protein-coding genes flags expressed(c,g)=1[S(c,g)>0] (>=1 completed transcript that generation). Emits two WIDE per-(seed,gen) matrices (one binary expressed, one raw synth_count; one column per gene, header=gene_id) plus per-gene and per-(seed,gen) metric tables. The _expressed matrix is the binary input the standalone uniqueness/operon CLIs consume.

status: REWRITTEN to use cohort def5_CI categories
description_and_math: Figures 5B/5E/5F/5G, with burn-in, using completed transcripts. NOW LABELS GENES WITH THE CANONICAL COHORT-WIDE def5_CI CATEGORIES read from sc.canonical_def5_classification() -- one level up from this multigen plotOut, since analysisMultigen appends the seed directory. It previously classified by the per-lineage POINT ESTIMATE (mean=0 / 0<mean<1 / mean>=1), which silently disagreed with every table: on sim set 1 that called 1652-1687 genes subgen per lineage where the cohort CI calls 1859 (~230-250 gene disagreement) and inflated never_expressed from 135 to ~330, because one lineage never fires many genes that some lineage does. The point estimate is still PRINTED as a diagnostic but labels nothing. Four categories now, colored from sc.PALETTE. The gene set is intersected with the def-5 gene key (is_mRNA covers ~4345 cistrons vs the 4309 protein-coding ones) and the drop count is printed, so figure and tables cover identical genes. Because categories are cohort-wide, all plotted lineages report the SAME counts -- that identity is the regression test. What still varies per lineage is the frequency scatter and the event raster. Plots the first N_LINEAGES_TO_PLOT=3 STRICT-successful lineages (seed-suffixed filenames) rather than seed 0 unconditionally. REQUIRES subgen_raw_extract.py to have run on the cohort; it now lives in sbatch job 02, not job 03.

Quantifies whether the SET of subgen genes expressed per cell is unique while the NUMBER is nearly constant: (A) per-cell count distribution vs the Poisson-binomial expectation, (B) distinct-set count and pairwise Jaccard vs an analytic independence null and a fixed-margins (curveball) null, (C) PCA of the cell x gene matrix, (D) population accumulation curve. Gene set from sc.load_def5_categories(pergene, category='subgen'). Was listed in cohort/__init__.py ACTIVE despite having no Plot class -- the parallel runner evaluates mod.Plot OUTSIDE its try/except (analysisBase.py:196), so that entry ABORTED the entire cohort analysis run at -c >1. Now unregistered and driven by sbatch job 04 instead.

Publication-ready 'clean' panels of the Figure-3 series in one visual style (editable-text PDF/PNG/SVG): count_distribution (per-cell number of subgen genes expressed, dashed mean line), jaccard (pairwise similarity over all cell pairs), and fig3B_heatmap (genes x cells binary heatmap, rows sorted by frequency, topped by a per-cell %-expressed bar) in black-and-white and color at each --n-cells. Note these three basenames are NOT subgen_-prefixed, unlike the rest of the family. Driven by sbatch job 04.

Operon membership of the subgen gene set: how many subgen genes are co-transcribed with others, to assess whether operon structure could confound the per-cell uniqueness/Jaccard analysis. Uses the cistron -> transcription-unit map from sim_data; a polycistronic TU (>=2 cistrons) is an operon. Documents how common operons are and lists memberships for the robustness check -- the mean pairwise cell-to-cell Jaccard is governed by each gene's population frequency and is invariant to within-cell co-transcription, so operons do not bias that statistic. Driven by sbatch job 04.

Operon-unit robustness check: recomputes the mean pairwise cell-to-cell Jaccard (and its independence and fixed-margins nulls) at the cistron level and at the operon-unit level, where co-transcribed subgen cistrons collapse into one unit (a unit is expressed if ANY of its subgen cistrons fired; units are connected components of the graph linking subgen cistrons that share a TU, handling overlapping TUs). If operons were inflating cell-to-cell similarity, collapsing them would pull the observed Jaccard toward its null. Driven by sbatch job 04.

'Protein memory': tests whether frequently-transcribed subgen genes rarely run out of protein, because long protein half-lives carry inherited protein through a generation that fails to transcribe. Both axes are per-lineage rates aggregated to a 95% CI (the def-5 estimator), so they are comparable and scale honestly with more seeds: y = protein-absence rate (expected fraction of cell-cycle TIME at zero copies, time-weighted per cell cycle, averaged within a lineage then across lineages) from _frac_protein_zero_per_cell.tsv; x = transcript-off frequency and def-5 rate from _synth_per_cell.tsv. Note its CIs are error bars on the plotted axes -- the CLASSIFICATION still comes from the per-gene table's category column. Strict filter inherited via the is_successful_lineage column. Driven by sbatch job 04.

Joins the per-gene protein-memory table to each protein's translation efficiency and degradation rate from sim_data, writes a self-contained interactive HTML scatter (hover for gene name, transcript-off frequency, protein-absence rate, def-5 rate, translation efficiency, half-life), and analyzes outliers -- especially genes ABOVE the y=x line, where protein is absent a larger fraction of time than the gene is transcriptionally off (the OPPOSITE of memory) -- testing whether short half-life and/or low translation efficiency explains them. Its thresholds are outlier thresholds, not subgen thresholds. Driven by sbatch job 04 (chained after subgen_protein_memory.py).

subgen_definition_used: Definitions 1-5 (pooled threshold sweep) PLUS the canonical def5_CI for comparison
description_and_math: Computes five pooled per-gene definitions on identical cells, each value=Sum_cells/n_cells, and sweeps thresholds [1.0,0.99,0.95] with subgen iff 0<value<t. def1 p_present (mRNA present), def2 p_any_init, def3 mean_init events, def4 p_any_synth (any completed transcript), def5 mean_synth (the pooled def5 value). description_and_math: Per-cell NET change in monomer count per generation: monomerCounts[last] - monomerCounts[first]. Row 0 is the daughter's inherited count (Listener.initialUpdate runs before the logger's first write, so it is a real state, not allocate() zeros) and the last row is the pre-division count, so this is a NET quantity -- synthesis minus degradation, which can be negative. Under balanced growth it is close to the inherited count, i.e. about half the final count; it is NOT gross synthesis. Cast to int64 before subtracting, since on an unsigned dtype the negative values this quantity depends on would wrap. There is no per-monomer count of COMPLETED proteins in the listeners (RibosomeData/didTerminate and actualElongations are scalars over all monomers); the nearest gross per-monomer quantity is RibosomeData/ribosome_init_event_per_monomer. Reads one cell at a time to keep rows paired with cell paths. Gene panel now from sc.curated_panel('curated10'). Strict filter.

Two per-gene quantities. Time-averaged synthesis probability: actual_rna_synth_prob(g)=(Sum_cells Sum_{t>0} p[t,g])/(Sum_cells (T_cell-1)), where p=actual_rna_synth_prob_per_cistron is already normalized to sum to 1 per timestep (fractional, not absolute). Per-generation existence: prob_mRNA_exists_in_gen(g)=(Sum_c 1[Sum_t mRNA_cistron_counts[t,g]>0])/n_cells.

SUPERSEDED by subgenerational_expression_table_def5.py. p_expressed = (cells with >=1 mRNA copy at some timestep)/n_cells; subgen iff 0 < p_expressed < 1 -- a point estimate against a threshold, with no confidence interval. Why superseded: (a) presence counts transcripts INHERITED from the mother and initiations later lost to tRNA attenuation, so almost every gene is 'sometimes absent' in some cell -- it called 3685 (set 2 v0) / 3194 (v1) genes subgen against 1859 for def5_CI, so the gene lists are NOT comparable; (b) the 'always on' count degrades as the cohort grows, the opposite of a per-lineage rate whose SE shrinks as std/sqrt(n_lineages); (c) DENOMINATOR BUG -- the read-failure handler continues without decrementing n_cells, so unreadable cells dilute every gene's probability; (d) uses the weak only_successful=True gate, not the strict filter. Its p_expressed value is recovered, more correctly, as p_mrna_present_def1 in the def5 table.
